caption: Mount
description: The Mount object describes a file system mount that makes a directory, file or volume available at a path inside a container, such as a bind mount of a host path, a named volume or a memory-backed file system. Mounts that expose sensitive host paths, for example the container runtime socket or the host root, can let a container escape to its host.
name: mount

host_path.description: The path on the host that is mounted, for a bind mount or a Kubernetes hostPath volume. For example: /var/run/docker.sock or /etc.

is_readonly.description: Indicates that the mount is read only inside the container. A writable mount of a host path lets the container change files on the host.

name.description: The name of the volume, if the mount has one. For example, the name of a named volume, or the name of a Kubernetes pod volume.

path.description: The path inside the container where the mount is attached. For example: /host or /var/run/docker.sock.

type.description: The mount type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the mount type.

1.caption: Bind
1.description: A directory or file from the host is mounted into the container, such as a bind mount or a Kubernetes hostPath volume. host_path holds the host path.

2.caption: Volume
2.description: Storage managed by the container runtime or the orchestrator is mounted, such as a named volume, or a Kubernetes persistent volume claim, emptyDir, configMap or secret volume.

3.caption: Temporary File System
3.description: A memory-backed temporary file system is mounted, which is not persisted on the host.

4.caption: Named Pipe
4.description: A named pipe from the host is mounted into a Windows container.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The mount type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

references.description: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, Baseline policy, HostPath Volumes
Docker Engine API, container inspect, Mounts (MountPoint)
